correspondence.finding: The selected beginning follows a short, unnamed western stream east into the directly labeled Nass. The map shows a separate Nass continuation arriving from the north; that unselected continuation is not substituted for the actual selected branch. Downstream, the selection follows the southeast-running Nass valley, with Konigus Creek and then Muskaboo Creek arriving from the west. The stream connection at the selected beginning is visible, although the feeder's own hydronym is not established.

The next two mainstem pieces follow the named Nass south, then around its prominent westward bend and southwestward continuation near the Taylor River approach, before running west to Bell-Irving. The shape and junction order match the selected route. Nearby Umma Lake and the surrounding lake chains are separate side settings, not names or passages transferred to the selected trunk.

The western chain begins on the small northwestern-turning headwater approach shown in the official map, then follows the directly labeled Bell-Irving River south and southwest before turning southeast through the Bell II corridor. It continues east of the Bowser Lake setting. Mehan, Oweegee and Hidden lakes are nearby side features; the selection does not take their lake bodies or the separate Bowser Lake route. An exact naming boundary at the small initial headwater segment is not inferred.

Below the Bowser approach, the second western piece continues along the labeled Bell-Irving, turns east and southeast past the separate Dog Lake setting, and joins Nass. This is a tributary component with its own hydronym, not an alias or an upper reach uniformly named Nass.

Below Bell-Irving the selected line follows the mapped Nass west briefly, then south and southeast past the Meziadin Lake approach and along the Cassiar Highway corridor. It bends southwest in the Cranberry River setting and continues down the labeled Nass through the Gitlaxksip and Aiyansh settings. Meziadin, Kwinageese, Kinskuch, Dragon and Lava lakes lie on separate approaches rather than on the selected line.

The final selected section continues southwest past Laxgalts'ap and ends in the broadened lower Nass channel, where the official map still prints Nass River. The regional overview places the adjoining coastal setting toward Nass Bay. The selected endpoint is upstream of much of that broad estuarine water, so it is not asserted to be a surveyed mouth or a river-to-bay naming boundary; the feature is not extended through Nass Bay or Portland Inlet.

The actual southwestern beginning follows an unnamed western feeder northeast toward São Sebastião do Umbuzeiro. The municipal map shows this connection to the town-side drainage and the impounded waterbody north of town, then a northeastern outlet labelled Riacho do Umbuzeiro. The western Zabelê/Dois Riachos approach is separate, and the printed river label within the impoundment is not a reservoir-name assignment.

The selected northeastern continuation corresponds to the basin map’s Rio Umbuzeiro approach, which joins the receiving Paraíba in the Congo/Caraúbas corridor. The report distinguishes Umbuzeiro and Sucuru as tributaries of Paraíba. The more northerly Monteiro–Poções–Camalaú approach is not the selected beginning and is not substituted because it is the main river in the report’s general description.

The selection then follows the Paraíba past the Caraúbas corridor into Epitácio Pessoa at Boqueirão through its southwestern river arm and out to the east. The report’s enlarged reservoir map distinguishes that arm from the separate western/northwestern contributing approaches. Taperoá is a separate northern tributary system rather than this selected headwater route.

Below Boqueirão, the actual southern arc and eastward continuation match the named middle Paraíba before the northward Acauã reservoir passage and lower outlet. The report separately identifies Acauã with Argemiro de Figueiredo in its figure title and maps the reservoir arms; Paraibinha remains a separate contributing river. Reservoir names and the Acauã–Araçagi canal are not adopted as uniform names or extra selected routes.

The lower northeast/east route matches the Paraíba through the Itabaiana/Pilar and Santa Rita setting. The actual endpoint is near the river’s turn into the broader Santa Rita/João Pessoa estuarine approach. The report maps and describes the downstream estuary continuing north to Costinha/Cabedelo; that complete northern estuary and Atlantic outlet lie beyond the selected line and are not claimed as included.

The selected southern beginning runs east through the small northeastern/eastern Guerrero watercourse at the Bachíniva boundary, then bends north into the southern Bachíniva valley. Guerrero and Bachíniva relief pixels support this connected approach. It is not the longer southern stream toward Agua Caliente or an El Chorro/La Matanza headwater substituted for the actual selected feeder. No separate hydronym or official source is assigned to the short initial stream.

The selected northward Bachíniva course passes through the mapped Presa Las Chepas corridor and continues north through the town-and-valley setting into the river labeled Santa María. The state sheet identifies the same reservoir as Constituyente Manuel M. Prieto (Las Chepas). Its storage-waterbody role remains separate from the river name. The mapped El Chorro, La Matanza, Guadalupe and La Casita tributary approaches are not selected replacement headwaters.

The route turns northwest into western Namiquipa and then follows the stream directly labeled Santa María between the western uplands and the Cerro La Mina/La Gorra setting. It continues toward the northwestern municipal margin and the El Tintero reservoir. The separate Santa Clara course farther east is not the selected river; nearby Laguna Prieta and Los Ajolotes are not assigned as selected lake passages.

The selected route enters El Tintero from the south, follows its elongated mapped reservoir corridor and continues north below its northern dam/outlet setting. The state original and southern Buenaventura relief sheet support this passage. The nearby western reservoir arms and the separate eastern Las Lajas reservoir are not additional selected approaches.

Below El Tintero, the line follows the western Buenaventura valley north through the San Buenaventura–La Merced setting into Galeana. The Galeana relief map directly labels the northward trunk Santa María and supports its bend eastward across the northern municipality. The model stays on the main valley route rather than entering the adjacent Ojo Caliente waterbody/side corridor, and it continues toward La Viñata and Los Valencia in the state cartography.

After the Galeana bend, the selected course turns northeast and north through the El Progreso–Cerro Madero and Colonia Cerro Blanco settings. The northern Buenaventura map labels the receiving course Santa María and distinguishes it from Los Jagüeyes and La Mula. The state sheet supports its continuation past El Vado Chico and Santa Rosa toward the Ascensión river corridor.

The final northward reach matches the Santa María river along the western side of Sierra China and enters the southern end of Laguna Santa María. The selected line then continues northwest within the elongated mapped lake corridor, with its endpoint in the lake setting rather than at an onward river outlet. Ascensión and state cartography separate this depression from Laguna de Guzmán, El Fresnal and adjacent eastern intermittent waters. No connection from the selected terminal to those waters is established.

The mountain beginning lies within the upper Kern corridor below the Kings-Kern Divide and north of Junction Meadow. The Forest Service study's Figure I-2 and appendix sheets E-1 through E-3 depict the near-southerly Kern River corridor past Junction Meadow and the separate Kern-Kaweah, Wallace, Whitney, Rock Creek and Big Arroyo approaches. The study calls the studied river North Fork Kern while the topographic base repeatedly labels it Kern River. The selected path follows this corridor rather than an eastern South Fork or a western tributary. The modeled start is not asserted to be the river's official source, and the more northerly Lake South America/headwater region is not automatically included.

The route continues through the upper-canyon Kern Lake and Little Kern Lake setting, then takes the distinctive eastward and southwestward turn around the Hockett Peak/Hole-in-the-Ground setting into Kern Flat. The separately drawn Little Kern River joins from the northwest at Forks of the Kern. Appendix sheets E-3 through E-5 directly show these relationships. The two mountain lake names are separate waterbody names, not aliases for the entire river; the generalized modeled line does not establish which precise parts of their changing shorelines or channels are crossed. The study also distinguishes the existing lakes from potential reservoirs shown as historical proposals.

South of Forks of the Kern, the selected river follows the Johnsondale Bridge, Fairview, Hospital Flat and Kernville corridor into the northern arm of Isabella Reservoir. The appendix sheets E-6 through E-8 show the river, separate flume/power structures and the reservoir setting. The KCWA map independently labels Kern River North Fork and the separate South Fork inflow from the east. The selection uses the northern arm and western outlet sector of Isabella, without selecting the full South Fork arm or treating the reservoir name as a river alias.

The KCWA original map depicts Kern River southwest from Isabella through its canyon and west through the Bakersfield area. The selected bends and valleyward turn agree at regional scale. KWBA Figure 2-3 distinguishes the winding river through the First and Second Point of Measurement corridor from the parallel Kern River/River Canal, Carrier Canal, Cross Valley Canal and other conveyances. The selection follows the river corridor to the Kern River-California Aqueduct Intertie setting; the nearby canal labels cannot be transferred to all upstream reaches.

At the southwestern turn the selection follows the northbound Outlet Canal/Kern River Flood Channel setting, continuing toward the Lost Hills and southern Tulare region. KWBA Figure 2-3 and Figure 3.6-3 explicitly separate the river, Outlet Canal, flood channel and California Aqueduct; their accompanying prose describes gated transfers and differing normal/high-flow routing. The EPA lowland map and DWR regional map distinguish the northbound flood conveyance from the separate aqueduct and adjacent irrigation network. This is positive evidence of engineered conveyance scope, rather than a natural-river name continuing merely because the model assigns a mainstem role.

Northward, the modeled route leaves the principal flood-channel approach and follows angular connections into the Tulare lake-bed network; the short second piece is an east-west continuation within that receiving setting. EPA Maps 4 and 5 show a dense major/minor canal grid, separate Tule River Canal and South Fork Kings River Canal approaches, and historical lake and flood-storage areas. These maps support the inland lake-bed correspondence but do not establish the entire selected continuation as a natural Kern River channel or establish one unique hydronym for every selected terminal segment. The modeled endpoint is neither an official river mouth nor proof of a continuous natural connection to the San Joaquin River.

scope_limit: MAIN_RIV groups and model mainstem roles do not establish a uniform name for every included reach, tributary or lake passage. Source observations support only the stated representative identity or hold.
publication_boundary: Own factual observations, attribution and official public URLs only; source originals, images, complete coordinates and private evidence remain omitted.
